overall_verdict: The no-pumping result is proved under equilibrium passivity and complete all-port accounting; it is standard thermodynamic structure, not claimed as novel. Shaat-Park's reversible Eq. (31) contradicts its reported nonzero closed-cycle work unless a work port or non-equilibrium/active source is omitted.

claims.claim: For a quasistatically equilibrated reversible passive material with a single-valued Helmholtz free energy, arbitrary internal coordinates, ideal unilateral frictionless contact, and all controlled coordinates/ports included, a closed complete-state cycle has zero net all-port work.
claims.proof: At equilibrium, dPsi=P dot dq+sum_j lambda_j dg_j. Complementarity and sustained ideal contact imply lambda_j dg_j=0 almost everywhere. Thus delta W_all,on=dPsi, and integration over a complete-state closed cycle gives zero.
assumptions: single-valued stored Helmholtz free energy for the complete system
complete internal state and contact/slider geometry return to the initial state
all external mechanical work ports are included
unilateral contact is ideal, frictionless, non-adhesive, and no finite-power impact occurs
claims.falsifier: Synchronized all-port raw data show closed-state net work outside propagated uncertainty while independently confirming reversible equilibrium, no omitted ports, and complete state return.
claims.costs: Analytical proof is O(number of generalized coordinates plus active contact constraints); physical validation requires calibrated force/torque and displacement/rotation histories at every port, state/contact observation, and uncertainty propagation.

claims.claim: Passive viscoelastic or frictional systems cannot deliver net work on a cycle returning their complete internal state; all-port work input equals nonnegative dissipation.
claims.proof: For an isothermal passive system, delta W_all,on=dPsi+delta D with delta D>=0. On a complete-state cycle W_all,on=D>=0; output work is therefore nonpositive.

claims.claim: The Shaat-Park 2023 source-free reversible cycle satisfies its stated Eq. (31) and yields nonzero net work with zero free-energy change.
evidence: Eq. (31), p. 14: delta W=dPsi for each reversible isothermal process; prose says the proposed passive solids always satisfy it.
Closed cycle returns to the stated zero-stress/reference state, so integral dPsi=0.
§4.1.2 and Fig. 5 report W approximately 16.6 kJ/m^3 for the favorable cycle and about -16 kJ/m^3 for another.
Eq. (32), p. 15, splits work into a potential differential and delta w_cn, which the authors state cannot be obtained from potential energy.
claims.resolution: At least one premise must be dropped: work is omitted at an actuator port; the constitutive contribution is active/non-equilibrium and not an equilibrium free-energy differential; the complete state is not closed; or the claimed cycle work is a modeling/accounting error.

claims.claim: The 2023 paper proves the rigid slider used to modulate circle profile contributes zero cycle work because endpoint stress is unchanged.
evidence: Appendix A.1 states that the slider mechanism is needed and moves rigidly up/down at states 3 and 4.
The paper infers zero energy contribution from unchanged stress state at the switch endpoints.
No slider actuator force/torque versus travel trace or integral is reported; the FEA energy check is described for deformation processes separately.
claims.valid_omitted_port: Generalized actuator work W_slider,on=sum_s integral F_s,specimen da_s, including all slider motions. Endpoint stress equality does not evaluate this path integral.
claims.qualification: The paper does not establish that slider work is nonzero; it also does not establish that it is zero. A measured nonzero value would explain output as externally driven work, while a rigorously zero value leaves the constitutive/Eq. (31) contradiction unresolved.

claims.claim: The reported approximately 16.6 kJ/m^3 cycle output is validated by public raw all-port physical data.
claims.evidence: The paper reports finite-element calculations and plotted increments (Appendix A.1 states N=40000); no raw all-port history for slider force/travel is available in the cited manuscript.
claims.falsifier: For the claimed output W_boundary,on=-16.6 kJ/m^3, measure W_slider,on and every other input port. A passive closed cycle requires W_slider,on+W_other,on=16.6 kJ/m^3+D, within uncertainty. Output with all measured input below that bound falsifies the source-free passive account; matching slider input identifies the drive.

claims.claim: Odd elasticity with nonzero closed-cycle work is already associated in primary literature with nonconservative/active interactions.
claims.evidence: Scheibner et al. state odd moduli are forbidden by energy conservation, derive cycle work proportional to enclosed strain-space area, and describe active bond forces.

claims.claim: A passive-component mechanical metamaterial can exhibit driven odd response when an external mechanical drive is explicitly applied.
claims.evidence: Rahimi and Park use periodically driven chiral gears, frictional tooth-wall contact, and detachment/recontact; the paper identifies the periodic mechanical loading as the input energy source.
claims.scope_limit: This is driven odd elasticity, not source-free equilibrium pumping; source is a 2026 arXiv preprint and reports FE simulations.

raw_channels: all boundary force and displacement histories
all boundary moment and rotation/spin histories
specimen-side slider force/torque and travel at every profile switch
all electrical, thermal, or chemical input ports
decisive_measurement.criterion: For reversible equilibrium, DeltaPsi=D=0 and R=0 within uncertainty. For passive dissipation D>=0 and all-port input equals D. A boundary output of 16.6 kJ/m^3 requires at least that much net positive slider/other input plus dissipation.

costs.source_computation: The primary paper uses a 4x4 lattice and 40000 increments per cycle. An auditable rerun adds slider degrees of freedom and exports force-travel, boundary work, internal energy, contact dissipation, and residual at each increment.
costs.physical_test: Requires an aluminum 4x4 sample and profiled sliders; translation/rotation stage; calibrated boundary load/torque and specimen-side slider sensors; DIC/contact observation; calibration coupons; repeats in both orientations; and propagated uncertainty. Dollar cost is unknown because fabrication and instrumentation choices are unspecified.
costs.evidence_limit: No physical all-port data or raw slider trace was located in the primary manuscript; no empirical result is claimed here.
